learning_outcomes.text: Consolidate the basic principles that govern the chemical reactivity of elements, especially of transition metals.
Acquire the knowledge necessary to understand the structure of inorganic complexes and the factors affecting their chemical stability.
Understand the physicochemical principles that characterize the growth and properties of inorganic supramolecular solids.
Development of interdisciplinary and critical thinking
Search for, analysis and synthesis of data and information, with the use of the necessary technologies
Production of free, creative and inductive thinking

syllabus_topics: Transition Elements: Electronic Configuration and Bonds
Coordination Chemistry: Rates and Mechanisms of Chemical Reactions
teaching_methods: Supportive learning through the use of multimedia (videos)
Supportive learning through valid online scientific sources

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination (for students with learning disabilities)

assessment_rules: Students are evaluated by an optional intermediate and a final written examination, which includes problem solving and developing topics. An oral examination is provided for students with learning disabilities. Students may view their exam scripts after results are published. Details on the evaluation process are available during the first lecture and on the course website.
